_about: WHAT A FACTION WANTS DECIDES WHERE ITS PARTIES GO (FACTIONS lane, row [wants send parties], 10/18; WORLD [parties move] BUY half). records/target/bb/factions.json already says what each of the demo factions (four, eight since FACTIONS [more banners] 10/18, twelve since FACTIONS [home bases] 10/18) WANTS (want.id). This file says, for each want, WHAT KIND OF PLACE OR GROUND that want sends a party at, and quotes the Battle Brothers line it is translated from. engine/bohemia_wants.js reads it; nothing here is a number (the row: 'no new numbers'): who goes first is the map's own distance, how many go is BohemiaTowns.REACH, the grounds are BohemiaBoardTerrain.KINDS. A modder edits this file to change where a faction's parties go (rule 38g). Page: records/BOHEMIA_FACTIONS_WHAT_A_FACTION_WANTS_DECIDES_WHERE_ITS_PARTIES_GO_10_18_26.md.

camps_harass_the_nearest_village.quote: You will face either Brigands or Zombies, whichever has a closer distance to the settlement.

a_spawnpoint_harasses_a_village.quote: if you destroy a spawnpoint that sends out parties to harass a village these raids will stop

raiders_live_off_the_trade_routes.quote: Killing of a spawnpoint of enemies close to trade routes will definitely help the villages as it reduced the frequency of caravans getting raided.

a_camp_grows_on_what_it_takes.quote: An Orc camp sends out raiders that successfully raid a couple of caravans and bring home a lot of supplies. Now the camp buys even more raiders so it can raid more caravans and so on.

the_roads_ambush.quote: which is the reason the AI prefers to lay in ambush in the forest tiles near roads

castles_patrol_the_roads.quote: the guard towers and castles send out patrols to secure roads and fight off bandits and other evil-doers

the_house_lives_on_its_supply.quote: watchtowers and castles rely on military supply caravans from towns and villages. If these get intercepted regularly the towers and castles also get into trouble.

the_dead_raid_for_corpses.quote: undead will not raid caravans for the money, but to create more corpses for their army

the_raid_leaves_the_place_raided.quote: This place has been recently raided! It's suffered damage, has lost valuable goods and supplies, and lives were lost.

beasts_roam.quote: Various wild beasts roam the lands.

a_raid_hits_the_attached_locations.quote: Defend a settlement against a single or multiple waves of enemies raiding their Attached Locations.

nomads_go_from_water_to_water.quote: They travel the barren desert from one source of water to the next

mercenaries_roam_for_contracts.quote: Various mercenary companies can be found roaming around on the Global map and are also actively looking for and accepting Contracts from settlements.

bounty_hunters_want_the_head.quote: They demand the bandit leader's head and attack if you refuse.

barbarians_roam.source: reference/library/grok/wiki/PAGES_ALL.tar.gz bb_all/0594_Dev Blog 116: The Barbarians, Part I.txt
barbarians_roam.quote: They roam the harsh and infertile lands as they have been for hundreds of years

barbarians_raid_the_settlement.quote: The barbarians attack you and want to raid the settlement that gave you the contract afterwards.

city_states_patrol.quote: Southern city states send regiments to patrol surroundings, and caravans to trade with other settlements.

militia_defend_their_homes.quote: If hostile troops raid a village or town, a group of militia soldiers spawn, ready to defend their homes and families.

goblins_hit_and_run.quote: Instead of brute force they usually ambush their enemies.

militia_gathered_when_sighted.quote: Militia forces can be gathered when a hostile party is sighted close to a settlement and disbanded again after the threat disappeared.

militia_is_the_settlement.quote: Each non-military settlement is a separate faction. They send caravans, peasants and, when enemies come close, can send militia squads to fight them.

hold-the-freeway.order: the trip: the map distance from the camp to the place plus the place's distance to the nearest freeway cell, shortest first; then nearer the camp; then by name
hold-the-freeway.why: the crew wants the freeway (VAMILY row [a house you give a fuck about]); Battle Brothers' raiders go at the nearest village and live off the trade routes, so a road crew goes at what stands nearest the freeway on its way, whatever its size: a camp by the road is the first thing a crew hits, never only the three fortresses

hold-the-depot.why: the house wants the depot (VAMILY row); Battle Brothers' castles patrol the roads their supply comes along, so the house's first party is a patrol on the nearest depot ground (industrial: the warehouse, the railyard, the storage lot), and the rest of its business is what the parties module already sends

finish-the-work.why: the dead's keeper wants to bring back what was left unfinished; Battle Brothers' dead raid for corpses, not money, so they go at the nearest place of any size, and a place already raided (our ruin is a condition, not a ground: bohemia_boardterrain NOT_ON_THE_MAP) goes first

keep-the-ground.why: the beasts want their ground and to be left alone; they never go at a place; a den already on its ground holds it (the patrol has arrived), a den off it walks to the nearest of it

hold-the-water.order: the trip: the map distance from the camp to the place plus the place's distance to the nearest pump or solar cell, shortest first; then nearer the camp; then by name
hold-the-water.why: the water people want the water; Battle Brothers' nomads are southern brigands who go from one water to the next, so they raid what stands nearest the pumps on their way, the road crews' rule with the water in place of the freeway

take-the-contract.why: the hired guns want to be paid; Battle Brothers' companies roam and take contracts from settlements, so a company's first party walks to the nearest ground with money on it (the Strip, the casino floor) to be hired, and the rest of its business is the parties module's

collect-the-head.why: the head takers want the crew boss's head; Battle Brothers' bounty hunters turn up where the bandits are and demand the leader's head, so their first party patrols the nearest road crews' ground (the freeway, the hills), never a settlement

gather-the-flock.why: the flock wants more of the people nobody counts; Battle Brothers' cultists are met only in two events and go at no settlement, so the flock holds the trailer park it gathers in, and a chapel off it walks to the nearest one

feed-the-herd.why: the keepers want the herd fed; Battle Brothers' barbarians are wildmen who roam and, crossed, 'want to raid the settlement', and every camp's raiders go at the nearest village, so the keepers go at the nearest place of any size, the dead's rule without the dead's taste for a place already raided: a herd eats wherever it is

guard-the-money.why: the eye in the sky wants the money kept where it is; Battle Brothers' city states send regiments to patrol their surroundings, so the security's first party patrols the nearest casino floor or Strip, a casino already on it holds it, and the rest of a settled seat's business is the parties module's

keep-the-block.why: the block watch wants the block left standing; Battle Brothers' militia only turn out when somebody raids their homes and never march on anyone, so the watch holds the nearest block of houses, a watch already on one stays, and it goes at no place

turns_out.why: FACTIONS [four seated] 10/18: Battle Brothers' militia have no seat of their own; every non-military settlement (a village, a town, never a castle) gathers them when a hostile party comes close and disbands them after. 'Close' has no number on the wiki, so ours is the crew's own mark: every town or camp a crew is going at gathers one watch party, standing on the place, wearing the watch's banner and defending the place's holder; a fortress has soldiers and never gathers one; a wild seat has no townsfolk. The disband is RUN's clock

hit-and-run.order: the trip: the map distance from the camp to the place plus the place's distance to the nearest lot or big-box cell, shortest first; then nearer the camp; then by name
hit-and-run.why: the runners want to hit and be gone; Battle Brothers' goblins ambush instead of fighting fair and every camp's raiders go at the nearest village, so the runners go at what stands nearest the open lots they ride, the road crews' rule with the lots in place of the freeway: in, out, across the lot

gaps: the region's wild row for ancient_dead (THE LOST CITY) carries no want in factions.json (the ancient dead are not one of the twelve), so it keeps the parties module's own choice; since FACTIONS [four seated] 10/18 every one of the twelve wants moves somebody: the keepers (Corn Creek) and the runners (Valley of Fire) are wild camps that send crews, the eye in the sky (Lake Las Vegas) a settled seat that patrols the money, and the block watch has no seat and turns out where crews go (keep-the-block turns_out); the hired guns roam without a base (region_bases.json roaming_without_a_base)

the valley's fourteen seats carry no want of their own (his canon graph's notes are not wants and this lane does not invent his factions' wants), so their crews still go at the worst canon feud's seat; the camps and towns become reachable through the wild crews that are handed in beside them

outside the valley the map's ground is RUN's region (slices/bohemia_region.js passAt: 1 is a road); the module takes the grounds as cells the caller hands it, so RUN adds the region's road cells as freeway and nothing here changes
